study type: secondary analysis of prospective, multicenter cohort study
exposure: fetal adiposity composite (fetal thigh adiposity and fetal abdominal wall thickness)
fetal adiposity composite > 90th centile vs. ≤ 90th centile
cohort: 2330 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancy in cephalic presentation
finding: Fetuses with a fetal adiposity composite > 90th centile were more likely to require Cesarean delivery than were those with adiposity composite ≤ 90th centile, even after adjusting for birth weight, maternal BMI, and need for induction of labor.
mod_finding: A fetal adiposity composite > 90th centile was not associated with an increased likelihood of operative vaginal delivery when compared with having an adiposity composite ≤ 90th centile.
